data.description: Armor is a category of items that provide players and mobs with some amount of protection from common types of damage. These items include helmets, chestplates, leggings, and boots, which can be placed in designated slots in a player's inventory.

From left (weakest) to right (strongest): no armor, <a href="/w/Leather_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Leather armor">leather armor</a>, <a href="/w/Copper_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Copper armor">copper armor</a>, <a href="/w/Golden_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Golden armor">golden armor</a>, <a href="/w/Chainmail_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Chainmail armor">chainmail armor</a>, <a href="/w/Iron_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron armor">iron armor</a>, <a href="/w/Diamond_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Diamond armor">diamond armor</a>, and <a href="/w/Netherite_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Netherite armor">netherite armor</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>note 1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup></figcaption></figure>
<p><b>Armor</b> is a category of items that provide <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">players</a> and <a href="/w/Mob" title="Mob">mobs</a> with some amount of protection from common types of <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a>. These items include <a href="/w/Helmet" title="Helmet">helmets</a>, <a href="/w/Chestplate" title="Chestplate">chestplates</a>, <a href="/w/Leggings" title="Leggings">leggings</a>, and <a href="/w/Boots" title="Boots">boots</a>, which can be placed in designated slots in a player's inventory.
</p>

<p><br>
</p><p>A full set of leather, copper, iron, golden, or diamond armor requires 24 units of a given material to craft. Netherite armor cannot be crafted directly, and is obtained by upgrading diamond armor in a smithing table. A turtle shell is a type of helmet, but no other armor items can be crafted from turtle scutes. Chainmail armor is not possible to craft, and can be obtained only from <a href="/w/Mob_drop" class="mw-redirect" title="Mob drop">mob drops</a>, <a href="/w/Trading" title="Trading">trading</a>, and <a href="/w/Generated_loot" title="Generated loot">generated loot</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Upgrading">Upgrading</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=5&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Upgrading" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section's source code: Upgrading"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Netherite armor is obtained by upgrading diamond armor in a <a href="/w/Smithing_table" class="mw-redirect" title="Smithing table">smithing table</a>. Each piece of netherite armor requires a <a href="/w/Netherite_ingot" class="mw-redirect" title="Netherite ingot">netherite ingot</a> and a <a href="/w/Netherite_upgrade_smithing_template" class="mw-redirect" title="Netherite upgrade smithing template">netherite upgrade smithing template</a>. A full set of netherite armor requires 4 netherite ingots and 4 netherite upgrade smithing templates.
</p><p>Netherite armor retains the <a href="/w/Enchantment" title="Enchantment">enchantments</a>, <a href="/w/Anvil_mechanics#Prior_work_penalty" title="Anvil mechanics">prior work penalty</a>, and number of <a href="/w/Durability" title="Durability">durability</a> points lost (instead of the remaining durability) from the <a href="/w/Diamond" title="Diamond">diamond</a> armor.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Mob_loot">Mob loot</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=8&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Mob loot" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section's source code: Mob loot"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><a href="/w/Zombie" title="Zombie">Zombies</a>, <a href="/w/Husk" title="Husk">husks</a>, <a href="/w/Zombie_villager" class="mw-redirect" title="Zombie villager">zombie villagers</a>, <a href="/w/Skeleton" title="Skeleton">skeletons</a>, <a href="/w/Stray" title="Stray">strays</a>, <a href="/w/Bogged" title="Bogged">bogged</a>, and <a href="/w/Piglin" title="Piglin">piglins</a> that spawn with armor have an 8.5% chance of dropping their armor when killed by the <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a>. The dropped armor has a random <a href="/w/Durability" title="Durability">durability</a> and retains any enchantments it has. All of the mentioned mobs except piglins can only spawn with armor in <a href="/w/Normal" class="mw-redirect" title="Normal">Normal</a> and <a href="/w/Hard" class="mw-redirect" title="Hard">Hard</a> difficulties. None of the mobs can naturally spawn with netherite armor.
</p><p>In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, <a href="/w/Pillager" title="Pillager">pillagers</a> and <a href="/w/Vindicator" title="Vindicator">vindicators</a> that spawn in <a href="/w/Raid" title="Raid">raids</a> have a small chance to drop an <a href="/w/Iron_helmet" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron helmet">iron helmet</a>, <a href="/w/Iron_chestplate" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron chestplate">iron chestplate</a>, <a href="/w/Iron_leggings" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron leggings">iron leggings</a>, or <a href="/w/Iron_boots" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron boots">iron boots</a>, in a badly damaged state, with a possibility of having a random enchantment.
</p><p>In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, armorer <a href="/w/Villager" title="Villager">villagers</a> throw chainmail armor to <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">players</a> who have the <a href="/w/Hero_of_the_Village" title="Hero of the Village">Hero of the Village</a> status effect.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Trading">Trading</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=9&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Trading" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section's source code: Trading"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Trading" title="Trading">Trading</a></div>
<p>Leather armor can be <a href="/w/Trading" title="Trading">bought</a> from leatherworker <a href="/w/Villager" title="Villager">villagers</a>. These armor pieces have randomly determined color.
</p><p>Iron armor, chainmail armor and enchanted diamond armor can be bought from armorer villagers.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Bartering">Bartering</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=10&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Bartering" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section's source code: Bartering"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><a href="/w/Piglin" title="Piglin">Piglins</a> may <a href="/w/Barter" class="mw-redirect" title="Barter">barter</a> <a href="/w/Iron_boots" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron boots">iron boots</a> enchanted with a random level of <a href="/w/Soul_Speed" title="Soul Speed">Soul Speed</a> when given a <a href="/w/Gold_ingot" class="mw-redirect" title="Gold ingot">gold ingot</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Fishing">Fishing</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=11&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Fishing" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=11" title="Edit section's source code: Fishing"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><a href="/w/Leather_boots" class="mw-redirect" title="Leather boots">Leather boots</a>, often badly damaged, can be obtained as a junk item from fishing.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Usage">Usage</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=12&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Usage" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=12" title="Edit section's source code: Usage"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Armor can be worn by a player or mob in order to protect them. See <a href="#Mechanics"><span style="white-space: nowrap;">§ Mechanics</span></a> for more details.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Equipping">Equipping</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=13&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Equipping" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=13" title="Edit section's source code: Equipping"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>A <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a> can equip a piece of armor by placing it in the correct slot in the <a href="/w/Inventory" title="Inventory">inventory</a>, by <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">using</span> it while it's in the main hand or offhand, or by <a href="/w/Dispenser#Behavior" title="Dispenser">dispensing</a> it from a dispenser onto themself. When <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">using</span> the armor piece, any equipped armor corresponding to the same slot is swapped out. Each armor piece fills one inventory slot, and armor pieces cannot be stacked.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Damage_reduction">Damage reduction</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=15&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Damage reduction" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=15" title="Edit section's source code: Damage reduction"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Wearing armor reduces incoming damage according to two values: <abbr title="armor points">armor</abbr>, and armor toughness. Each piece of armor provides a given <abbr title="armor points">armor</abbr> and armor toughness value, and the values from each armor piece are added together when calculating damage reduction.
</p><p>The strength of incoming damage also determines the damage reduction of worn armor, as armor does not protect in a linear fashion, and instead drops off more and more as incoming damage increases. For example, a full set of diamond armor reduces the damage of a zombie's attack by 77%, but reduces the damage of a piglin brute's attack by only 67%. The total damage reduction of armor cannot drop off below 20% of its maximum.
</p><p>The location of a given armor piece does not affect its damage reduction. For example, wearing leggings applies its damage reduction to the whole body, not just the player's legs.
</p><p>The following tables represent the damage reduction of the different armor types depending on the incoming damage, accounting for armor toughness:

<p>Armor, also known as armor points, represents the base defensive value of worn armor. The total number of armor points that the player has is the sum of the armor points of the individual pieces of armor worn, and is visually represented by the armor bar. The armor increases the player's <code>armor</code> attribute while worn. Armor points determine the minimum amount of damage armor reduces. See <a class="mw-selflink-fragment" href="#Damage_formulas">Damage formulas</a> below to see how damage reduction is calculated.
</p><p>The <code>armor</code> attribute is capped at 30. If commands are used to give the player armor with more than 30 armor points, or to set the player's <code>armor</code> attribute above 30, damage is calculated as if the player had 30 armor points. The armor bar does not show armor points above 20.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Armor_toughness">Armor toughness</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=17&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Armor toughness" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=17" title="Edit section's source code: Armor toughness"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="" src="/images/Disambig_color.svg?2db52" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="12" height="9" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="444" data-file-height="340"></span></span> "Toughness" redirects here.  For the property of <a href="/w/Blocks" class="mw-redirect" title="Blocks">blocks</a>, see <a href="/w/Hardness" class="mw-redirect" title="Hardness">Hardness</a>.</div>
<p>Armor becomes less effective for higher damage values, reducing the damage by smaller and smaller percentages until it reaches the minimum percentage. Armor toughness mitigates this behavior to a degree. The amount of damage reduced still decreases for higher damage values, but not as much. The total number of armor toughness the player has is the sum of the armor toughness of the individual pieces of armor worn. Armor toughness does not have a visual indicator like armor points. Armor increases the player's <code>armor_toughness</code> attribute while worn. See <a class="mw-selflink-fragment" href="#Damage_reduction">Damage reduction</a> above to see how armor toughness affects damage calculation.
</p><p>Only <a href="/w/Diamond_Armor" title="Diamond Armor">diamond</a>, <a href="/w/Netherite_Armor" title="Netherite Armor">netherite</a> and <a href="/w/Wolf_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Wolf armor">wolf armor</a> have armor toughness.
</p><p>The <code>armor_toughness</code> attribute is capped at 20. If commands are used to give the player armor with more than 20 armor toughness, or to set the player's <code>armor_toughness</code> attribute above 20, damage is calculated as if the player has 20 armor toughness.
</p><p>The following table shows the amount of armor toughness given by armor that can be worn by the player.
</p>

<p>Since without <a href="/w/Command" class="mw-redirect" title="Command">commands</a>, the toughness of 20 is impossible, this can be simplified to:
</p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">(</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">(</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>𝖺</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝗆</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝖯</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗂</mi><mi>𝗇</mi><mi>𝗍</mi><mi>𝗌</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>𝖺</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝗆</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝖯</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗂</mi><mi>𝗇</mi><mi>𝗍</mi><mi>𝗌</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">−</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>𝖽</mi><mi>𝖺</mi><mi>𝗆</mi><mi>𝖺</mi><mi>𝗀</mi><mi>𝖾</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>𝗍</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗎</mi><mi>𝗀</mi><mi>𝗁</mi><mi>𝗇</mi><mi>𝖾</mi><mi>𝗌</mi><mi>𝗌</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">)</mo></mrow><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">)</mo></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math>
</p><p>This gives a base damage reduction of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>𝖺</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝗆</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝖯</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗂</mi><mi>𝗇</mi><mi>𝗍</mi><mi>𝗌</mi></mrow></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math>, a minimum damage reduction of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>𝖺</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝗆</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝖯</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗂</mi><mi>𝗇</mi><mi>𝗍</mi><mi>𝗌</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math>, and a maximum damage reduction of 80%. With 0 armor toughness, the base damage reduction decreases by 2% per point of damage. With 8 or 12 armor toughness, the base damage reduction decreases by 1% and 0.8% respectively.
</p><p>We can use this equation to define the <i>breaking point</i> of armor:
</p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>𝖡</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝖾</mi><mi>𝖺</mi><mi>𝗄</mi><mi>𝗂</mi><mi>𝗇</mi><mi>𝗀</mi><mi>𝖯</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗂</mi><mi>𝗇</mi><mi>𝗍</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>𝖺</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝗆</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗋</mi><mi>𝖯</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗂</mi><mi>𝗇</mi><mi>𝗍</mi><mi>𝗌</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>𝗍</mi><mi>𝗈</mi><mi>𝗎</mi><mi>𝗀</mi><mi>𝗁</mi><mi>𝗇</mi><mi>𝖾</mi><mi>𝗌</mi><mi>𝗌</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math>
</p><p>The value of the breaking point represents the amount of damage required to reach the minimum damage reduction value, which is also the point at which armor toughness no longer applies. The formula above can alternatively be rewritten as:
</p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" class="mwe-math-element mwe-math-element-inline"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>e</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mtext> </mtext><mi <p>These <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> values are lower if a <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a> wears pieces of diamond or netherite armor or has toughness added to the armor through <a href="/w/Commands" title="Commands">commands</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Damage_sources">Damage sources</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=19&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Damage sources" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=19" title="Edit section's source code: Damage sources"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>The following types of <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> are reduced by armor and, consequently, damage the armor itself:
</p>
<ul><li>Direct (melee) attacks from <a href="/w/Mob" title="Mob">mobs</a> and <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">players</a>. This includes the <a href="/w/Strength" title="Strength">Strength</a> and the <a href="/w/Weakness" title="Weakness">Weakness</a> effects and damage-increasing enchantments.</li>
<li>Getting hit with an <a href="/w/Arrow" title="Arrow">arrow</a>, a <a href="/w/Shulker_bullet" class="mw-redirect" title="Shulker bullet">shulker bullet</a> or a thrown <a href="/w/Trident" title="Trident">trident</a>. This includes extra damage from enchantments (except shulker bullets).</li>
<li>Getting hit with a <a href="/w/Fireball" title="Fireball">fireball</a> from a <a href="/w/Ghast" title="Ghast">ghast</a> or <a href="/w/Blaze" title="Blaze">blaze</a>, or a <a href="/w/Fire_charge" class="mw-redirect" title="Fire charge">fire charge</a>.</li>
<li>Laser beam of a <a href="/w/Guardian" title="Guardian">guardian</a> or an <a href="/w/Elder_guardian" class="mw-redirect" title="Elder guardian">elder guardian</a>.</li>
<li>Damage from <a href="/w/Thorns" title="Thorns">Thorns</a> enchantment, or spikes of <a href="/w/Guardian" title="Guardian">guardians</a> and <a href="/w/Elder_guardian" class="mw-redirect" title="Elder guardian">elder guardians</a>.</li>
<li>Touching a damaging block (<a href="/w/Fire" title="Fire">fire</a>, <a href="/w/Lava" title="Lava">lava</a>, <a href="/w/Magma_block" class="mw-redirect" title="Magma block">magma block</a>, <a href="/w/Cactus" title="Cactus">cactus</a> or <a href="/w/Sweet_berry_bush" class="mw-redirect" title="Sweet berry bush">sweet berry bush</a>).
<ul><li>This excludes netherite armor which is not damaged by fire-related sources.</li></ul></li>
<li>Touching a <a href="/w/Pufferfish" title="Pufferfish">pufferfish</a>.</li>
<li><a href="/w/Explosion" title="Explosion">Explosions</a>.</li>
<li><a href="/w/Firework" class="mw-redirect" title="Firework">Fireworks</a> with at least a <a href="/w/Firework_star" class="mw-redirect" title="Firework star">firework star</a> in the recipe.</li>
<li><a href="/w/Lightning" class="mw-redirect" title="Lightning">Lightning</a>.</li>
<li>Getting hit with a falling <a href="/w/Anvil" title="Anvil">anvil</a>.</li>
<li>Getting hit with a <a href="/w/Snowball" title="Snowball">snowball</a> from a <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a>​<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement applies only to upcoming versions of Minecraft.">upcoming:</span> <a href="/w/Java_Edition_Combat_Tests" title="Java Edition Combat Tests">JE Combat Tests</a></i>]</sup> or <a href="/w/Snow_golem" class="mw-redirect" title="Snow golem">snow golem</a>.​<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><a href="/w/Special:TalkPage/Armor" title="Special:TalkPage/Armor"><span title="dispensers?" style="border-bottom: 1px dotted">more information needed</span></a></i>]</sup></li>
<li>Getting hit with an <a href="/w/Egg" title="Egg">egg</a> from a <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a>​<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement applies only to upcoming versions of Minecraft.">upcoming:</span> <a href="/w/Java_Edition_Combat_Tests" title="Java Edition Combat Tests">JE Combat Tests</a></i>]</sup></li></ul>
<p>The following types of damage are <b>not</b> reduced by armor and have no effect on the armor itself:
</p>
<ul><li>Ranged sonic boom attacks from the <a href="/w/Warden" title="Warden">warden</a>.</li>
<li>Fall damage (including using <a href="/w/Ender_pearl" class="mw-redirect" title="Ender pearl">ender pearls</a>).</li>
<li>Ongoing damage from being on <a href="/w/Fire" title="Fire">fire</a>.</li>
<li><a href="/w/Suffocating" class="mw-redirect" title="Suffocating">Suffocating</a> inside a block or due to <a href="/w/Entity_cramming" class="mw-redirect" title="Entity cramming">entity cramming</a> (also includes the <a href="/w/World_border" title="World border">world border</a>)‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">JE</a>  only</span></i>]</sup>.</li>
<li><a href="/w/Drowning" class="mw-redirect" title="Drowning">Drowning</a> in water (partially for <a href="/w/Turtle_shell" class="mw-redirect" title="Turtle shell">turtle shells</a>).</li>
<li><i><a href="/w/Starvation" class="mw-redirect" title="Starvation">Starvation</a>.</i></li>
<li>Colliding with a block while flying with <a href="/w/Elytra" title="Elytra">elytra</a>.</li>
<li class="mw-empty-elt"></li>
<li>Magic (<a href="/w/Evoker" title="Evoker">Evoker</a> fangs, <a href="/w/Status_effect" class="mw-redirect" title="Status effect">status effects</a> and <a href="/w/Instant_damage" class="mw-redirect" title="Instant damage">instant damage</a> from a <a href="/w/Potion_of_Harming" title="Potion of Harming">potion of Harming</a> or <a href="/w/Dragon%27s_Breath" title="Dragon's Breath">Dragon's Breath</a>) (but <a href="/w/Protection" title="Protection">Protection</a> does reduce magical damage.)</li>
<li><i>Falling into the <a href="/w/Void" title="Void">void</a> or <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/kill" title="Commands/kill">kill</a></span></code>.</i></li>
<li>Being inside of a <a href="/w/Powder_snow" class="mw-redirect" title="Powder snow">powder snow</a> block.
<ul><li>This excludes if the player or mob wears any piece of leather armor.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p>All the types of damage that are <b>not</b> <i>italicized</i> can be reduced by the <a href="/w/Protection" title="Protection">protection</a> enchantments.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Knockback_resistance">Knockback resistance</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=20&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Knockback resistance" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=20" title="Edit section's source code: Knockback resistance"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Knockback_resistance" class="mw-redirect" title="Knockback resistance">Knockback resistance</a></div>
<p>Each <a href="/w/Netherite" class="mw-disambig" title="Netherite">netherite</a> armor piece gives a <a href="/w/Knockback_resistance" class="mw-redirect" title="Knockback resistance">knockback resistance</a> of 1 (10%), which results in a <a href="/w/Knockback_(mechanic)" title="Knockback (mechanic)">knockback</a> reduction of 40% with a full set. The <a href="/w/Blast_Protection" title="Blast Protection">Blast Protection</a> enchantment can be applied to armor to increase the user's <a href="/w/Explosion_knockback_resistance" class="mw-redirect" title="Explosion knockback resistance">explosion knockback resistance</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Enchantments">Enchantments</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=21&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Enchantments" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=21" title="Edit section's source code: Enchantments"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">See also: <a href="/w/Enchantment" title="Enchantment">Enchantment</a> 
</div>
<p>Armor can be enchanted to provide various benefits. Enchantments can provide more protection or allow armor to resist certain types of <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> that armor doesn't normally protect against, such as fall damage or <a href="/w/Fire" title="Fire">fire</a>. Damage reduction from enchantments does not decrease the armor's <a href="/w/Item_durability" class="mw-redirect" title="Item durability">durability</a>. Armor enchantments do not appear on the armor bar. The strength of enchantments received through an enchanting table is dependent on the armor piece's <a href="/w/Enchantability" class="mw-redirect" title="Enchantability">enchantability</a>.
</p><p>As with several enchantments, several different levels of protection are possible. The maximum level of a protection enchantment is IV (4). Protection enchantments from multiple pieces of armor stack together.
</p><p>Each protection enchantment protects against specific types of <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a>. The amount of damage reduction depends on the <b>Enchantment Protection Factor (EPF)</b> provided by that enchantment.
</p>

<p>When a <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a> or <a href="/w/Mob" title="Mob">mob</a> wearing armor is subjected to <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a>, the EPFs of all applicable enchantments are added together, having a maximum of 20, and a minimum of 0 (when the game is calculating the reduced damage). The damage reduction is <code>resultingEPF / 25</code>, giving a minimum reduction of 0 and a maximum reduction of <sup>4</sup>⁄<sub>5</sub> or 80%. This means the <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a> cannot be immune to <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> from <a href="/w/Projectile" title="Projectile">projectile</a> or <a href="/w/Explosion" title="Explosion">explosion</a> in a <a href="/w/World" title="World">world</a> without cheating, even if they wear armor with the maximum level of relevant enchantments on each part.
</p><p>Because of the caps in the calculation, it is possible to achieve maximum protection against specific types of damage with just three pieces of armor. For example, two pieces of armor with <a href="/w/Blast_Protection" title="Blast Protection">Blast Protection</a> IV (EPF 8 each) and a single piece with <a href="/w/Protection" title="Protection">Protection</a> IV (EPF 4) would give a total EPF of 20 versus explosions. Any additional EPF would be wasted against explosions (but might be useful against other types of damage, if applicable).
</p><p>If the <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> is of a type that armor protects against normally, this reduction applies only to the damage that got through the armor. 
</p><p>It is possible using <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/give" title="Commands/give">give</a></span></code> to obtain armor with an <a href="/w/Enchantment" title="Enchantment">enchantment</a> level higher than what is normally obtainable via normal <a href="/w/Survival" title="Survival">survival</a>. Using this method, a <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a> could give themselves, for example, a full set of diamond armor with a <a href="/w/Protection" title="Protection">Protection</a> V enchantment on every piece. Following the algorithm above, we find that, because Protection V has an EPF of 5, the armor reaches the maximum EPF of 20 for all types of damage. Any higher Protection enchantments could be used to reach the cap with just one level XX (20) enchantment, rather than having a full set of enchanted armor, but would be wasted if all pieces shared the same level enchantment.

<p>Only one form of protection can be applied to a piece of armor (i.e. a chestplate cannot have both Fire Protection and Blast Protection, unless using <a href="/w/Command" class="mw-redirect" title="Command">commands</a> to get all protection enchants in one piece of armor). Feather Falling, Frost Walker, Depth Strider, and Soul Speed are enchantments applicable only to boots. Respiration and Aqua Affinity are enchantments applicable only to helmets. Swift Sneak is an enchantment applicable only to leggings.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Durability">Durability</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=22&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Durability" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=22" title="Edit section's source code: Durability"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Any hit from a <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> source that can be blocked by armor removes one point of <a href="/w/Durability" title="Durability">durability</a> from each piece of armor worn for every 4<span class="hidden-alt-text">HP</span><span class="nowrap mc-hearts"><span class="iconbar pixel-image nowrap" style="--icon-offset:-1px;" title="2 hearts"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="❤️" src="/images/Heart_%28icon%29.png?faf83" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="9" height="9" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="9" data-file-height="9"></span></span><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="❤️" src="/images/Heart_%28icon%29.png?faf83" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="9" height="9" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="9" data-file-height="9"></span></span></span></span> of incoming damage (rounded down, but never below 1). 
</p><p>The chart below shows the <a href="/w/Durability" title="Durability">durability</a> per unit of material for each piece of armor, compared to that of the <a href="/w/Boots" title="Boots">boots</a>. The durability per unit does not depend on the tier of the armor.
</p>

<p>This means that for the same number of <a href="/w/Leather" title="Leather">leather</a>/<a href="/w/Iron_ingot" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron ingot">iron ingots</a>/<a href="/w/Gold_ingot" class="mw-redirect" title="Gold ingot">gold ingots</a>/chainmail/<a href="/w/Diamond" title="Diamond">diamond</a>, <a href="/w/Boots" title="Boots">boots</a> can take 1.5 more damage than leggings. Thus, <a href="/w/Chestplate" title="Chestplate">chestplates</a> and <a href="/w/Leggings" title="Leggings">leggings</a> offer more defense points per unit, but have less <a href="/w/Durability" title="Durability">durability</a> per unit.

<p>Armor worn by a non-<a href="/w/Player" title="Player">player</a> mob does not lose durability when attacked by any means. Helmets that are worn by undead <a href="/w/Mob" title="Mob">mobs</a> lose durability when exposed to <a href="/w/Sunlight" class="mw-redirect" title="Sunlight">sunlight</a> due to absorbing the mob's <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> from sunlight. Every tick where the mob would normally be set on fire, the helmet has a 50% chance to lose 1 durability.
</p><p>Netherite armor does not lose durability from <a href="/w/Lava" title="Lava">lava</a> or <a href="/w/Fire" title="Fire">fire</a> damage.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Mob_interactions">Mob interactions</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=23&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Mob interactions" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=23" title="Edit section's source code: Mob interactions"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<dl><dt>General</dt>
<dd>Wearing a mob <a href="/w/Head" title="Head">head</a> in the helmet armor slot reduces the distance the corresponding mob detects the player by 50%, with the exceptions being the <a href="/w/Wither_skeleton_skull" class="mw-redirect" title="Wither skeleton skull">wither skeleton skull</a><sup id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><a href="/w/Special:TalkPage/Armor" title="Special:TalkPage/Armor"><span title="Verification needed for Bedrock Edition">verify for Bedrock Edition</span></a></i>]</sup> and <a href="/w/Dragon_head" class="mw-redirect" title="Dragon head">dragon head</a>.</dd></dl>
<dl><dt><a href="/w/Creaking" title="Creaking">Creakings</a></dt>
<dd>A player wearing a <a href="/w/Carved_pumpkin" class="mw-redirect" title="Carved pumpkin">carved pumpkin</a> in the helmet slot does not cause creakings to become immobile when looking at them.</dd></dl>
<dl><dt><a href="/w/Endermen" class="mw-redirect" title="Endermen">Endermen</a></dt>
<dd>A player wearing a <a href="/w/Carved_pumpkin" class="mw-redirect" title="Carved pumpkin">carved pumpkin</a> in the helmet slot does not aggravate endermen by looking at them.</dd></dl>
<dl><dt><a href="/w/Piglin" title="Piglin">Piglins</a></dt>
<dd>While the player is wearing at least one piece of gold armor, <a href="/w/Piglin" title="Piglin">piglins</a> behave as neutral mobs instead of hostile. <a href="/w/Piglin_brute" class="mw-redirect" title="Piglin brute">Piglin brutes</a> do not become neutral and remain hostile.</dd></dl>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Block_interactions">Block interactions</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=24&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Block interactions" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=24" title="Edit section's source code: Block interactions"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<dl><dt><a href="/w/Powder_snow" class="mw-redirect" title="Powder snow">Powder snow</a></dt>
<dd>Players and mobs can't freeze in powder snow while wearing at least one piece of leather armor. They also do not sink in powder snow while wearing leather boots, and the player can move through the powder snow like <a href="/w/Scaffolding" title="Scaffolding">scaffolding</a>.</dd></dl>
<dl><dt><a href="/w/Magma_block" class="mw-redirect" title="Magma block">Magma blocks</a> and <a href="/w/Campfire" title="Campfire">campfires</a></dt>
<dd>A player wearing boots enchanted with <a href="/w/Frost_Walker" title="Frost Walker">Frost Walker</a> does not take damage while standing on magma blocks or lit campfires.</dd></dl>
<dl><dt><a href="/w/Soul_sand" class="mw-redirect" title="Soul sand">Soul sand</a> and <a href="/w/Soul_soil" class="mw-redirect" title="Soul soil">soul soil</a></dt>
<dd>A player wearing boots enchanted with <a href="/w/Soul_Speed" title="Soul Speed">Soul Speed</a> gains a speed boost when moving on soul sand and soul soil blocks.</dd></dl>
<dl><dt><a href="/w/Water" title="Water">Water</a></dt>
<dd>A player wearing boots enchanted with <a href="/w/Frost_Walker" title="Frost Walker">Frost Walker</a> converts nearby water source blocks into <a href="/w/Frosted_ice" class="mw-redirect" title="Frosted ice">frosted ice</a>.</dd></dl>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Locator_bar">Locator bar</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=25&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Locator bar" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=25" title="Edit section's source code: Locator bar"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Wearing <a href="/w/Head" title="Head">heads</a> or <a href="/w/Carved_pumpkin" class="mw-redirect" title="Carved pumpkin">carved pumpkins</a> hides the player from the <a href="/w/Locator_bar" class="mw-redirect" title="Locator bar">locator bar</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Repairing">Repairing</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=26&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Repairing" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=26" title="Edit section's source code: Repairing"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Item_repair" title="Item repair">Item repair</a></div>
<p>Armor, like tools and weapons, can be repaired by placing two pieces of the same type (e.g., iron helmets) in a <a href="/w/Grindstone#Repairing_and_disenchanting" title="Grindstone">grindstone</a> or in the crafting grid.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading5"><h5 id="Unit_repair">Unit repair</h5><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=27&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Unit repair" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=27" title="Edit section's source code: Unit repair"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Anvil_mechanics#Unit_repair" title="Anvil mechanics">Anvil mechanics § Unit repair</a></div>
<p>A piece of armor can be repaired in an anvil by adding units of the armor <a href="/w/Material" class="mw-redirect" title="Material">material</a>'s repair material, with each repair material restoring 25% of the armor item's maximum durability, rounded down. Chainmail armor can be repaired in an anvil using <a href="/w/Iron_ingot" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron ingot">iron ingots</a>, and netherite armor can be repaired in an anvil using <a href="/w/Netherite_ingot" class="mw-redirect" title="Netherite ingot">netherite ingots</a>.
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Dyeing_leather_armor">Dyeing leather armor</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=28&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Dyeing leather armor" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=28" title="Edit section's source code: Dyeing leather armor"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Dye#Dyeing_armor" title="Dye">Dye § Dyeing armor</a></div>
<ul><li>In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, leather armor can be dyed by <a href="/w/Crafting" title="Crafting">crafting</a> it together with 1 or more dyes.</li>
<li>In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a>, leather armor can be dyed by <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">using</span> it on a <a href="/w/Cauldron" title="Cauldron">cauldron</a> filled with dyed water. This consumes 1 layer of water but does not change the color of the water.
<ul><li>Dyed leather armor also be undyed by <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">using</span> it on a cauldron with undyed water. This changes the water's color to the color of the armor's dye, and changes the leather armor to have no dye color.</li></ul></li></ul>
<p>Default color hex code for leather armor is <span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: #A06540; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> #A06540</span>.
<span class="anchor" id="Dye_calculator"></span>
</p>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Armor_trims">Armor trims</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=29&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Armor trims" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=29" title="Edit section's source code: Armor trims"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Smithing#Trimming" title="Smithing">Smithing § Trimming</a></div>
<p>Armor can be given trims using an armor trim smithing template, a trim material and any armor piece. Trimmed armor has different patterns and different colors depending on the template and material used.

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Mob_armor">Mob armor</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=31&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Mob armor" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=31" title="Edit section's source code: Mob armor"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Armor_equipped_on_mobs">Armor equipped on mobs</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=32&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Armor equipped on mobs" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=32" title="Edit section's source code: Armor equipped on mobs"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Geared_mobs" title="Geared mobs">Geared mobs</a></div>
<p><span class="anchor" id="Mob_armor"></span>
</p><p>Some mobs have a chance to spawn with armor equipped. When a mob spawns with armor, the number of pieces of armor, the type of armor pieces, and whether the armor is <a href="/w/Enchanted" class="mw-redirect" title="Enchanted">enchanted</a>, depends on the <a href="/w/Difficulty" title="Difficulty">difficulty</a>; although, the tier of armor (leather, gold, etc.) has a fixed probability. Mobs can spawn with trimmed armor when spawned from an <a href="/w/Ominous_trial_spawner" class="mw-redirect" title="Ominous trial spawner">ominous trial spawner</a>. Some mobs also have a chance to spawn with the ability to pick up armor on the ground and equip it. ​<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><a href="/w/Special:TalkPage/Armor" title="Special:TalkPage/Armor"><span title="updated chances in The Copper Age, including copper armor" style="border-bottom: 1px dotted">more information needed</span></a></i>]</sup>
</p>

<p>It is impossible for zombies, skeletons, and their variants to naturally spawn with <a href="/w/Turtle_shell" class="mw-redirect" title="Turtle shell">turtle shells</a>, netherite armor, or <a href="/w/Mob_head" class="mw-redirect" title="Mob head">mob heads</a>. 
</p><p>The protection provided by armor and armor <a href="/w/Enchantment" title="Enchantment">enchantments</a> works the same for <a href="/w/Mob" title="Mob">mobs</a> as it does with <a href="/w/Player" title="Player">players</a>.

<li><span class="nowrap"><span class="sprite-file" style=""><span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/w/Vindicator" title="Vindicator"><img alt="" src="/images/EntitySprite_johnny.png?6d568" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="16" data-file-height="16"></a></span></span><a href="/w/Vindicator" title="Vindicator"><span class="sprite-text">Vindicator</span></a></span>‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup></li></ul>
<p>These mobs do not spawn with armor and it cannot be equipped in <a href="/w/Survival" title="Survival">Survival</a> mode, but if equipped with <a href="/w/Commands" title="Commands">commands</a>, their armor is visible:
</p>
<ul><li><span class="nowrap"><span class="sprite-file" style=""><span class="pixel-image" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/w/Giant" title="Giant"><img alt="" src="/images/EntitySprite_zombie.png?ce11f" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="16" data-file-height="16"></a></span></span><a href="/w/Giant" title="Giant"><span class="sprite-text">Giant</span></a></span>‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup></li></ul>
<p>All other mobs can be equipped with armor via commands, but the armor cannot be seen.
</p><p>A <a href="/w/Helmet" title="Helmet">helmet</a> protects a mob that burns in <a href="/w/Sunlight" class="mw-redirect" title="Sunlight">sunlight</a> (mainly <a href="/w/Undead" title="Undead">undead</a> mobs) from burning, but this depletes the helmet's <a href="/w/Durability" title="Durability">durability</a> as it absorbs the <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a>. Eventually, the helmet loses all of its durability and breaks, and then the mob burns in the sunlight. A <a href="/w/Carved_pumpkin" class="mw-redirect" title="Carved pumpkin">carved pumpkin</a>, <a href="/w/Mob_head" class="mw-redirect" title="Mob head">mob head</a>, or anything placed into the head slot using commands, can also protect the mob from burning in sunlight. These do not have a durability and as such cannot break.
</p><p>Damage caused by any other source does not cause a mob's armor durability to decrease, unless the armor is <a href="/w/Wolf_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Wolf armor">wolf armor</a>.
</p>

<p><a href="/w/Horse_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Horse armor">Horse armor</a> can be equipped on a <a href="/w/Horse" title="Horse">horse</a> to protect it from most forms of <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a> similarly to player armor. Horse armor does not have a durability and does not break. Golden horse armor is more protective than iron horse armor.

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Wolf_armor">Wolf armor</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=36&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Wolf armor" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=36" title="Edit section's source code: Wolf armor"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Wolf_Armor" title="Wolf Armor">Wolf Armor</a></div>
<p><a href="/w/Wolf_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Wolf armor">Wolf armor</a> can be equipped on a tamed <a href="/w/Wolf" title="Wolf">wolf</a> to protect it from most forms of <a href="/w/Damage" title="Damage">damage</a>, including ones that normal armor does not protect against such as <a href="/w/Fall_damage" class="mw-redirect" title="Fall damage">fall damage</a> and burning. Wolf armor functions differently than player armor and horse armor. Instead, it absorbs all damage it protects against, and decreases its durability by the number of points of damage absorbed. The armor can be repaired using <a href="/w/Armadillo_scute" class="mw-redirect" title="Armadillo scute">armadillo scutes</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Nautilus_armor">Nautilus armor</h4><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=37&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Nautilus armor" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=37" title="Edit section's source code: Nautilus armor"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">Main article: <a href="/w/Nautilus_Armor" title="Nautilus Armor">Nautilus Armor</a></div>
<p><a href="/w/Nautilus_armor" class="mw-redirect" title="Nautilus armor">Nautilus armor</a> can be equipped on a tamed <a href="/w/Nautilus" title="Nautilus">nautilus</a> to protect it from most forms of damage.
Like horse armor, nautilus armor does not have a durability and does not break. Golden nautilus armor is more protective than iron nautilus armor. 
</p>

</div>
<div class="treeview">
<ul><li><span title="NBT Compound / JSON Object"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-48px -16px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[NBT Compound / JSON Object]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> components</span>: the item's <b>components</b> tag.
<ul><li><span title="Int"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-48px -0px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[Int]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> minecraft:dyed_color</span>: The RGB color of the tint applied to a dyed item, typically as a result of combining the item with dyes in a <code>minecraft:crafting_dyed</code> type crafting recipe. More generally, this component is used as the <code>minecraft:dye</code> color provider in <a href="/w/Item_model_definition" class="mw-redirect" title="Item model definition">item model definitions</a> (so only item models that explicitly use this color provider will be tinted). If present on an item, gray text is added to the tooltip showing either an italic "Dyed" when <a href="/w/Advanced_tooltips" class="mw-redirect" title="Advanced tooltips">advanced tooltips</a> is <i>off</i>, or a non-italic "Color: #<code><hex color code></code>"<sup id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>note 3<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> instead when <a href="/w/Advanced_tooltips" class="mw-redirect" title="Advanced tooltips">advanced tooltips</a> is <i>on</i>. The color is stored as an integer which packs the color's red, green and blue channels using this formula:<br><code>(<span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: Red; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> Red</span> <abbr title="Logical left shift"><<</abbr> 16) + (<span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: Green; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> Green</span> << 8) + <span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: Blue; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> Blue</span></code><sup id="cite_ref-23" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-23"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>note 4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <iframe id="mcw-calc-mfxv3" class="mcw-calc searchaux" data-type="decimalColor" src="https://tools.minecraft.wiki/static/tools/decimalColor/#?id=mfxv3&locale=en&url=https%3A%2F%2Fminecraft.wiki%2Fw%2FArmor" allow="accelerometer 'src'; clipboard-write 'src'; encrypted-media 'src'; fullscreen 'src'; picture-in-picture 'src'; autoplay 'src'" allowfullscreen="" style="border-width: medium; border-style: none; border-color: currentcolor; border-image: none; display: block; width: 100%; color-scheme: auto;"></iframe></li>
<li><span title="NBT List / JSON Array"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-32px -32px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[NBT List / JSON Array]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> minecraft:dyed_color</span>: An alternative format. A list of 3 floats, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 (inclusive)<sup id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>note 5<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>, corresponding to the red, green and blue channels of the color. This format is automatically packed into the integer format by multiplying each float by 255, converting them to unsigned bytes (equivalent to taking the floor and then applying modulo 256), then using the formula <code>-16777216 + (<span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: Red; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> Red</span> << 16) + (<span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: Green; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> Green</span> << 8) + <span style="white-space: nowrap;"><span style="display: inline-block; background-color: Blue; border: 1px solid #888; border-radius: 0.3em; color: transparent; width: 1em; height: 1em; vertical-align: -0.36em; margin-right: -0.1em"><br></span> Blue</span></code> due to the alpha channel being implicitly set to 255, resulting in a negative integer.<sup id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>note 6<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>.</li></ul></li></ul>
<ul><li><ul><li><span title="NBT Compound / JSON Object"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-48px -16px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[NBT Compound / JSON Object]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> minecraft:trim</span>: Contains the trim applied to this <a class="mw-selflink selflink">armor</a> piece. If present on an item, information about the armor trim is added to the item's tooltip.
<ul><li><span title="String"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-32px -16px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[String]</span></span><span title="NBT Compound / JSON Object"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-48px -16px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[NBT Compound / JSON Object]</span></span><span class="nowrap" style="font-weight: bold;"> pattern</span>: One <a href="/w/Trim_pattern_definition" class="mw-redirect" title="Trim pattern definition">trim pattern</a> (an <span title="String"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-32px -16px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[String]</span></span> <a href="/w/Resource_location" class="mw-redirect" title="Resource location">ID</a>, or a new <span title="NBT Compound / JSON Object"><span class="sprite nbt-sprite" style="background-position:-48px -16px;background-size:64px auto;height:16px;width:16px"></span><span class="hidden-alt-text">[NBT Compound / JSON Object]</span></span> trim pattern definition).

</td></tr><tr class="collapsible-row">
<td>Leather armor is now <a href="/w/Crafted" class="mw-redirect" title="Crafted">crafted</a> with leather instead of <a href="/w/Cloth" class="mw-redirect" title="Cloth">cloth</a>.</td></tr><tr class="collapsible collapsible-rows"><th class="historytable-subheader" colspan="8" style="border-bottom: none"><span class="collapsetoggle" style="min-width: 40.4688px;">[<span class="jslink" tabindex="0">hide</span>]</span><a href="/w/Java_Edition_version_history" title="Java Edition version history"><i>Java Edition</i></a></th></tr><tr class="collapsible-row"><th class="nowrap" rowspan="5" colspan="3"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_1.0.0" title="Java Edition 1.0.0">1.0.0</a></th><th colspan="4" rowspan="2"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_Beta_1.9_Prerelease" title="Java Edition Beta 1.9 Prerelease">Beta 1.9 Prerelease</a></th>
<td>The armor protection behavior has been changed. Previous to this update, the total armor protection is based in this equation: (<i>total equipped armor damage reduction</i> − 1) × ((<i>total equipped armor max durability</i> − <i>total equipped armor damage</i>) ÷ <i>total equipped armor max durability</i>) + 1, where “1” is the minimum amount of damage reduction before a piece of armor breaks. Armor no longer reduces certain damage types to be covered by enchantments. Basically, before this, taking damage would decrease the durability (depleting the armor bar), and the lower the durability, the lower the protection amount.
</td></tr><tr class="collapsible-row">

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Trivia">Trivia</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Armor?section=52&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Trivia" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Armor?action=edit&section=52" title="Edit section's source code: Trivia"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<ul><li>Considering all 29 armor pieces, 16,777,216 colors of dyed leather armor, 18 armor trims, 11 trim materials, every durability level of each armor piece and every survival-obtainable combination of armor enchantments, the total number of armor pieces obtainable in survival is 40,139,103,939,010,560 or 40 quadrillion.
<ul><li>Helmets have 20,480 enchantment combinations, chestplates have 2,560, leggings have 10,240, and boots have 153,600.</li></ul></li></ul>

<li id="cite_note-1"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><a href="#cite_ref-1" aria-label="Jump up" title="Jump up">↑</a></span> <span class="reference-text">The <a href="/w/Turtle_shell" class="mw-redirect" title="Turtle shell">turtle shell</a> is not pictured. The turtle shell is between iron and diamond, having equal armor points and greater <a href="/w/Durability" title="Durability">durability</a> than iron, but less than diamond.</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-20"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><a href="#cite_ref-20" aria-label="Jump up" title="Jump up">↑</a></span> <span class="reference-text">Piglins spawn naturally only with gold, although other armor types can be picked up.</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-22"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><a href="#cite_ref-22" aria-label="Jump up" title="Jump up">↑</a></span> <span class="reference-text">The hexadecimal number is always at least 6 digits (with leading zeroes if needed), with additional digits if the alpha channel is included, despite the alpha channel having no effect on the tint color.</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-23"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><a href="#cite_ref-23" aria-label="Jump up" title="Jump up">↑</a></span> <span class="reference-text">For positive values larger than <samp>0x00FFFFFF</samp>, the most significant byte encodes the alpha channel (opacity), however this is effectively ignored when providing the tint color to the item model, as the tint does not affect opacity.</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-24"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><a href="#cite_ref-24" aria-label="Jump up" title="Jump up">↑</a></span> <span class="reference-text">Float values outside of this range are accepted, but clamped from 0 to 255 by modulo 256 after being multiplied by 255. For example, -1.0 is equivalent to 0.00392156862 (or 1/255).</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-25"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><a href="#cite_ref-25" aria-label="Jump up" title="Jump up">↑</a></span> <span class="reference-text">This can result in an item that is not normally obtainable and it affects the hexadecimal code that is shown in the (advanced) tooltip. For example <code>dyed_color=0x000000</code> shows "#000000" but <code>dyed_color=[0,0,0]</code> shows "#FF000000" despite them both representing the same pure black RGB color.</span>
</li>
</ol></div>
